transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the production policy review on August 25, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the process. I'll be making the final decision on the rate-limit policy that gets communicated to customers, but before I do, I need each of your teams to report your release-impacting findings. To recap where the draft stands: we're looking at 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, the same limit applied to authentication endpoints, and no staffed launch window specified. I'd like to hear from backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations on any concerns or findings before I record the final policy. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share a release-impacting finding from backend engineering. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Our load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I hadn't updated the draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this is critical for the review.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this contractual notice requirement needs to be factored into our launch timing and customer communications.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. This is lower than the 100 requests per minute currently in the draft, and applying the same 100 RPM limit to auth endpoints would leave them vulnerable to credential-stuffing attacks. The finding isn't in the security tracker yet because the investigation is still being closed, but this needs to be reflected in the final policy before it goes to customers.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from support operations. We confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan yet because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated, but this is our only available staffed launch window and it needs to be factored into the final policy and launch timing.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Update the ordinary API-key limit to 150 RPM with a 60-second burst window per backend engineering's load replay findings.
Set authentication endpoint limit to 30 RPM per API key per security's credential-abuse investigation findings.
Send contractual notice to Acme by September 1 to permit enforcement on September 15, and factor the 14-day notice requirement into all customer communications.
Schedule staffed launch during the 10:00-12:00 UTC window on September 15 with documented escalation handoff.
Ensure all findings are entered into their respective trackers and the product launch ticket before the final policy is recorded.
